column1: # The shared front end's early-error codes, mapped onto this family's diagnostic registry
# Written: 2026-10-20, at milestone SJL-12 (task SJL-12.3), under JSD-0080 decisions D13, D31 and D37.
# Checked by: eng/check-frontend-mapping.py, part E of docs/evidence/sjl-12-001/decision-rule-area.md.
# WHAT THIS FILE DECIDES. Which registry code each shared code (JSEnnnn) of the catalogue becomes in
# this family, and which of those codes reach a registry row under a meaning the row does not
# publish. It changes no registry row: the registry stays at revision 18 (D13). A meaning the
# registry does not publish is recorded here as a split candidate, and SJL-13 gives it a new number
# under JSD-0009. A number is never given a changed meaning.
# TWO KINDS OF ROW, one table, LF, no quoting, `-` for "does not apply".
# - kind `registry`: one row per code of the registry's embedder-seam half. `meaning` quotes the
#   row's published meaning: its code and name as registry.txt publishes them, and its declaration's
#   which registry.txt names as the half's declaration). `conditions` lists the catalogue's message
#   identifiers (its conditions) that published meaning covers. `row` names the catalogue's
#   engine-only row (EX) that explains the code where one does, `-` where none does. `notes` says how
#   the meaning is read where the reading matters.
# - kind `code`: one row per shared code of the catalogue, in the catalogue's order. `row` is its
#   catalogue row and `conditions` that row's message identifier.
#   `wide_codes` and `slice_codes`: the registry codes the rule reaches today on each path, from the
#   catalogue row's site cells and the sites the catalogue's completeness report
#   (docs/evidence/sjl-12-001/catalogue/vm-sites.tsv in Broiler.JS) assigns to the row, each opened at
#   sites-read-at; `manifest` where the slice refuses the construct by manifest (2104,
#   SliceStaticSemantics.cs:607) before the rule can apply; `none` where the path accepts; `-` where
#   it refuses with no registry code of its own (a run-time step, or the evaluated source's own code).
#   `registry_code`: the one registry code the shared code maps to.
#   `relation`: `within-meaning` when the registry row's published meaning covers the rule, and then
#   `meaning` quotes it exactly as the registry row does; `split` when the code reaches the row under a
#   meaning the row does not publish, and then `meaning` names the row it leaves, the meaning, and
#   that the new number is minted at SJL-13 under JSD-0009.
#   `other_codes`: every other registry code the rule reaches today, ` | `-separated, each `split`
#   (the shared code splits registry rows there: from SJL-13 it reaches only its registry code, or a
#   number SJL-13 mints for the fact) or `other-row` with the catalogue row whose refusal it is.
# HOW A MEANING IS READ. A rule is within a row's meaning when it refuses the kind of fact the row's
# name and declaration state, wherever in the source the fact occurs: an escape in a template or an
# identifier is the escape 2005 names, a parameter bound twice is a name declared twice in one
# scope (2201), and `yield` used as a name in a generator is a word the context reserves (2209).
# It is split when the row is reached by a different kind of fact. 2101's meaning is its stage's,
# the parser's, as D13 reads it: the token at which the wide parser, with the contexts and checks it
# carries while parsing, cannot continue; a 2101 the lowering reports after a complete parse is not
# that. So every row the lowering refuses with 2101 is split from it, and `return` outside a
# function body is one: the wide parser carries no [Return] context and admits it (ParseReturn,
# JsParser.cs:2117-2131), and the lowering refuses it (JsCompiler.Exceptions.cs:261). D13 names
# `new.target` with the lowering's uses: the parser refuses it first, and the lowering's second
# check is the binder's from SJL-12.6, so its rows are split too.
# WHERE D13'S SPLIT CANDIDATES ARE. 2206 for undeclared private names and for `arguments` in fields:
# the split rows EE0167, EE0177, EA0009, EX0031 and EE0130, EE0138, EA0005. 2402 for duplicate
# import-attribute keys: EE0180. 2207 for `return`: the split row EX0033, `return` in a class static
# block (JsCompiler.Exceptions.cs:275), which D12 keeps coded 2207. 2104 for `await`, `using` and a
# logical assignment: the other_codes of EE0140 and EX0008, of EP0006 to EP0008, and of EE0035. 2203
# for destructuring without an initialiser: EX0009's other_codes. 2101 from the binder: the split
# rows for `super`, `return` (EX0032, `return` outside a function body, JsCompiler.Exceptions.cs:261),
# `new.target` and regular-expression patterns. The two `return` conditions are catalogue rows of
# their own by the owner's decision of 2026-10-20, which leaves D13 as written. A split row beyond
# D13's list says "found by this mapping"; an other code beyond it carries no "(D13)".
# The catalogue copy part E checks is the file catalogue-copy names, byte-identical to
# catalogue-path at catalogue-commit; eng/check-frontend-mapping.py refuses a copy whose SHA-256 is
